source.title: The large learning rate phase of deep learning: the catapult mechanism
source.authors: Aitor Lewkowycz; Yasaman Bahri; Ethan Dyer; Jascha Narain Sohl-Dickstein; Guy Gur-Ari

record.file_problem: Full paper and supplementary material are present; no apparent cutoff or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: The paper directly tests the learning-rate training dynamics and catapult behavior described in V5, including loss, curvature and divergence across learning rates.
record.gate_note: Results cited from prior work are not rows. The plotted training accuracies in Figure S6 are included only as figure-only observations; the text does not give precise values.
record.test_reason: The study directly analyzes and measures V5's catapult dynamics under squared loss: initial loss growth, decreasing NTK curvature, subsequent convergence, and failure at larger learning rates. It is an original source for V5, so no V5 verdict labels are assigned. Its CIFAR training-accuracy plots also bear on V1, but the supplied text does not establish their distance from zero classification error.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate: under MSE, sufficiently wide networks can recover from learning rates above the initial linearized stability limit through a short loss increase and curvature reduction, then converge to low loss and flatter minima. Excessive rates generally prevent training; the single-sample ReLU example fails through dead neurons rather than divergence. The authors also report that catapult-phase rates often improve generalization.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes gradient descent theoretically and tests the dynamics empirically with MSE and SGD; V5’s reported wide-network result is consistent with this, while the practical experiments include stochastic SGD settings.
record.method_sensitivity: Learning rate changes the outcome: below ηcrit the dynamics are lazy, in the catapult range loss can rise before convergence, and above ηmax training diverges. The paper reports that activation and architecture affect ηmax; ReLU networks have an empirical maximum near 12/λ0, while tanh is closer to 4/λ0.
record.problems: Only one initialization is considered in most experiments; the authors say they did not hyperparameter tune learning rates or L2 regularization. Some training-accuracy results are presented only as plots, with no precise values in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant numerical training-error rows were recoverable from the plots beyond the figure-only training-accuracy rows R5–R6.

untested.parts: Random or corrupted labels, model-size comparisons, and systematic early-stopping or regularization comparisons. Near-zero classification error cannot be determined from the supplied textual rendering of Figure S6.
Teacher-student ReLU local-minimum frequencies and the effect of one or two extra student neurons.
Depth-induced training degradation and matched comparisons with identity shortcuts or special initialization.
Comparative initialization effects on training speed and trainable depth; orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization.
Long-time full-batch sharpness hovering at the stability threshold and divergence despite initialization below that threshold.
Matched training-speed and learning-rate comparisons with and without batch normalization, including Fixup.

missing.what: The single-sample, two-hidden-layer ReLU model fails above approximately 12/λ0 by dead neurons producing f=0, rather than by loss divergence. This distinguishes failure mechanisms at excessive learning rates.
The two-hidden-layer tanh MNIST network has ηcrit = 0.06 and a maximum stable rate closer to 4/λ0, contrasting with approximately 12/λ0 for ReLU.
Additional WRN curvature sweeps test robustness to L2 regularization and NTK parameterization: Figure S9 uses L2 = 0.0005 and ηcrit = 0.18; Figure S11 uses NTK normalization and ηcrit = 31.47.
missing.locator: Supplement C.3 and C.5; Figures S9 and S11

record.verdict_notes: V5 labels are withheld because this study is an explicitly identified original source. No V1 label is justified without readable training-accuracy values. NTK curvature should not be silently equated with the exact Hessian sharpness used in later edge-of-stability claims.

versions.untested_parts: The paper plots training accuracy for CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, but does not report readable values establishing near-zero classification error; it does not test random or corrupted labels or compare model sizes.
Does not test sharpness hovering at the stability threshold over long full-batch training, or runs that diverge despite starting below the threshold.

rows.value: For ηcrit < η < ηmax, loss rises before converging to zero; for η > ηmax, loss diverges. ηcrit ≈ 1.
rows.note: The text describes the phase behavior; Figure 2 plots the example dynamics.
rows.check: The listed learning rates describe the example trajectories, not the complete sweep establishing divergence. Attribute the divergence region to Figure 2c and Section 2.1.3; the theoretical thresholds are 2/λ0 and 4/λ0.

rows.value: Error grows initially; curvature decreases until λt < 2/η, after which error converges to zero.
rows.note: The result is an analysis of the paper’s theoretical model, not an empirical benchmark run.
rows.check: This is a theoretical large-width analysis, with training time allowed to grow logarithmically with width. State ηmax = 4/λ0 for this linear-activation model; do not present convergence as an unrestricted empirical result for arbitrary finite-width datasets.

rows.measure: Early training loss and NTK curvature
rows.value: For ηcrit < η < 4/λ0, curvature decreases below 2/η and the loss initially increases before converging; the transient takes less than 10 steps.
rows.note: The paper says the observed maximum learning rate for these ReLU experiments is approximately 12/λ0.
rows.check: Add MSE loss and batch size 512. The listed rates span lazy and catapult conditions; initial loss growth applies to the rates above ηcrit = 6.25.
